_README: Selectors that can be gutted to a constant without any test noticing.
DISCOVERED, NOT DESIGNED. These are PRE-EXISTING debt, not caused by the PR
that surfaced them.
RULES:
· A survivor NOT listed here FAILS the build. New debt is blocked.
· A listed entry that no longer survives ALSO fails, with instructions to
delete it. The list cannot rot into a permanent allowlist the way an
unchecked exemption file does.
· Adding an entry is a visible diff in a PR. That is the point: it should
cost a reviewer's attention, not be a silent escape hatch.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT A FIX: each of these needs a non-empty control on the
population its guard actually scans, which is a judgement per guard, not a
sweep. Holding an unrelated PR hostage to that work would be the wrong trade;
leaving the tool non-blocking would be worse, because a check that cannot
fail is the defect this whole tool exists to find.
TWO CLAIMS THIS FILE USED TO MAKE, BOTH CORRECTED 2026-09-17:
· It said the first sweep covered 12 guards and that '12 of 12 files had
at least one'. Only 7 files were ever listed. Either the sweep was 7 or
five entries were dropped; the record does not say, so the count is no
longer asserted here.
· It said 'its 506 guards'. The population is 621 .test.ts files across
tests/guards + tests/guardrails, measured.
THE LAST TWO ENTRIES WERE INVISIBLE UNTIL THE TOOL COULD SEE THEM.
parcel-authoring-coverage and generated-columns both reported ZERO candidates
under the old line-based scanner — a clean bill of health from an audit that
examined nothing — because its describe/it gate matched RegExp.prototype.test
and doc-comment prose, then never decremented. generated-columns:walk survives
EVERY gut the tool has. Neither is new debt; both are newly VISIBLE debt, and
the rest of the 286 selectors the rewrite recovered have not been swept.
UPDATED 2026-09-19 by the #971 guardrails sweep (102 files).
· parcel-authoring-coverage:walk REMOVED — it now has a control, per rule 3.
The tool confirms: 'all 2 selector(s) have teeth'.
· module-import-boundaries:scan ADDED, and it is the one case in the sweep
where a control is not possible today rather than merely absent.
`classify` sorts src/app-layer into agri / core / platform. Measured:
28 / 0 / 291. CORE_RE matches compliance, vendor and the audit-CYCLE
domain, all of which the GRC teardown deleted. So the ratchet polices a
seam with ONE SIDE, BASELINE is empty, and the tree has zero violations
— `scan() -> []` is therefore indistinguishable from 'correctly found
nothing' BY ITS RESULT. No assertion can separate them without a fixture
tree the guard has no way to accept.
What IS asserted instead, in the file: the traversal is real (>200
repo-relative .ts files, the agri side present, sources carrying imports
the scanner's own regex matches), `resolveImport` maps the specifier
shapes, `baselineKey` distinguishes edges, and — pinned at zero — that
the core side is empty. That last one FAILS the moment a core file
returns, which is the signal to delete this entry and give `scan` a
real control, because the ratchet will finally have something to find.
Review when that happens, or 2026-12-19, whichever comes first.
The other 17 findings from that sweep are NOT here: each got a real

control instead. A baseline entry is the exception, not the pattern.

  UPDATED 2026-09-19 by the #971 tests/guards sweep.
    · e2e-isolation:scan ADDED — the SECOND case where a control is not
      possible rather than merely absent, and it fails the same way
      module-import-boundaries:scan does.

      `scan()` returns [] TODAY because no spec offends: BASELINE is empty
      and the tree is clean. So the `[]` gut REPRODUCES THE TRUE VALUE and
      is not a mutation of this program at all — a failed probe, not a hole
      found. Eight of the nine guts (0, false, null, undefined, {}, '', Set,
      Map) have no `.filter`/`.map` and throw at the consuming seam, so ONE
      of nine survives, and that one is degenerate.

      A control cannot close it here: the only thing that reddens a gutted
      `scan()` is a real offending spec ON DISK, and planting one under
      tests/e2e mid-run hands every sibling guard that walks that directory
      a transient file.

      What IS asserted instead, in the file: the chain re-runs over the same
      corpus and reports a real count of spec files, test spans and candidate
      bindings, each CLEARED by detectCascade, plus the same chain FLAGGING a
      cascade planted into real spec source. Delete this entry the moment a
      genuine offender lands — the guard will finally have something to find.
      Review then, or 2026-12-19, whichever comes first.
